headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Claude Code can write/modify the shared workspace and git while awesome-selfhosted is a read-only knowledge list, so prompt-injection and leakage are limited but workflow corruption is plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no execution or ingestion surface, so it cannot be hijacked directly. B can read files and stdin/stdout, and its shared-state path is filesystem/git, so only a manual or file-based bridge exists. That makes injection possible only through unusual operator-mediated copy/paste or shared files, not by default.
conditions: IF the operator copies A-generated text into files or stdin that B treats as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF B is pointed at a shared workspace containing attacker-controlled markdown or prompts, B may follow them.
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of B's prompt/files unless reviewed.
Use a separate directory for B's work.
Disable automatic ingestion of repository docs as instructions where possible.
Add a human review step before B executes any file-derived instruction.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not a leakage source. B can read/write local files and has broad network egress, but the pair only overlaps if the operator places sensitive files in B's workspace. With A being a static list, the leakage blast radius is small and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in B's cwd or user-provided directories, B can exfiltrate them over network egress.
IF A is used as a source of links that lead B to sensitive local paths, leakage risk increases only through operator action.
mitigations: Do not mount secrets in B's working directory.
Run B in a dedicated non-sensitive repo.
Block outbound network except approved endpoints during review tasks.
Strip secrets from any files B may read.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no write surfaces, so it cannot conflict operationally. B can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. The pair therefore has a real default conflict risk only on B-side multi-instance use, but A does not contribute writes.
conditions: IF two B instances operate on the same repo without locking, git and file conflicts can occur.
IF the operator expects A to coordinate writes, that expectation is false because A is not runnable.
mitigations: Use one B instance per repo.
Enable git locking or a single-writer workflow.
Separate branches per task.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static knowledge-management list and does not generate authoritative facts or actions. B can act on file contents, but there is no documented pipeline where B consumes A's output as trusted input. Any cascade would require the operator to manually turn A's content into instructions, so the default risk is limited.
conditions: IF the operator pastes A-derived recommendations into B without verification, B may execute them.
IF A's directory listing is treated as an authoritative policy source, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Verify any A-derived guidance before acting in B.
Require a second source for operational decisions.
Keep A as reference-only, not as an instruction feed.
Have B summarize before executing changes.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source directory with no touched data classes or egress, so it presents no residency or retention issue on its own. B handles source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, and its docs show Anthropic API use plus user-configured MCP servers. Compliance risk exists only if regulated data is placed into B's workspace or sent through those services.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in B's cwd or sent to configured MCP/API endpoints, retention/residency obligations may be triggered.
IF the operator uses B on PHI or EU PII without a matching policy, compliance gaps arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B's workspace.
Review MCP server destinations before enabling them.
Use redacted samples for coding tasks.
Confirm retention settings for any connected service.
